A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same controlled study of scaling and primate visual alignment. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and Brain-Score evaluation of over 600 models, fitted scaling relationships, and supplementary training-objective experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original model-training and alignment results and reports additional dataset experiments and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The core architecture-scaling, neural readout, power-law fitting, and compute-allocation procedures remain unchanged. SimCLR, DINO, and FGSM fine-tuning already appeared in v1 Appendix D; their expanded treatment does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: v3 Figure 3 and Appendix B add CIFAR-10 low-resolution object images and infiMNIST handwritten digits, substantially extending the training distributions examined. ImageNet21k-P, WebVision-P, iNaturalist, and Places365 were already represented in v1 Figure 3; their new descriptions are documentation additions.

E2.justification: The pretrained comparison is substantially revised: v1 Appendix B reports 121 models, versus 94 in v3 Appendix D. AlexNet, ConViT, and EfficientViT disappear from the corresponding plotted comparator families. v3 additionally identifies evaluated CLIP and DINOv2 models and comparisons with ImageNet-fine-tuned counterparts. The principal controlled architecture comparison remains stable.

E3.justification: The added CIFAR-10 experiment uses class-balanced subsets of 10–3,000 images per class and full-dataset runs lasting 100, 250, 1,000, and 2,500 epochs. These introduce additional sampling and training-budget conditions. The existing ImageNet/EcoSet training recipes, readout splits, and alignment metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond relocating existing experiments, v3 adds separate neural and behavioral SimCLR scaling fits, region-specific SimCLR compute curves, neural-versus-behavioral trained/random comparisons, and a ViT-S regional training-objective breakdown (Figures 7a and S4–S6). These substantially deepen tests of saturation and architectural initialization effects.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three seeds for selected dataset sizes, ten cross-validation repetitions, and 1,000 bootstrap resamples producing 95% confidence intervals. Correlation significance reporting also persists. Changed correlation coefficients, p-values, and fitted intervals are result revisions rather than changes in statistical practice.

E6.justification: Many plotted results and fitted relationships change. Figure 3a's ImageNet/EcoSet ceilings change from 0.47/0.50 to 0.46/0.48; average public/private agreement changes from R2 = 0.95 to 1.00 (v1 Figure 7; v3 Figure S1). Added CIFAR-10/infiMNIST curves and revised pretrained and training-objective comparisons substantially alter the result record, without establishing same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, power-law forms, compute assumptions, and allocation equations remain substantively unchanged. Reversing the residual sign in Equation 6 leaves the symmetric Huber objective equivalent. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain behavioral improvement versus neural saturation, greater benefits from data scaling, architectural effects on efficiency, and stronger scaling benefits higher in the visual hierarchy. Removing the abstract's allocation-recipe sentence does not remove that contribution, which remains in the results.

C2.justification: v3 removes the Platonic-representation interpretation and develops explanations involving saturation under self-supervision, objective-dependent learning dynamics, and recurrence's diminishing sample-efficiency advantage. Figure 3 recasts Places365's shortfall in terms of specialized distributions rather than image quality. The limitations also correctly acknowledge the already-tested recurrent CORnet-S architecture.

D1.justification: New Appendices A–B substantially document previously underspecified auxiliary experiments: software libraries, ResNet18 use on additional datasets, dataset pruning and resulting sizes, and new dataset construction and training schedules. The main text newly specifies ten epochs of FGSM fine-tuning. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously used procedures; the code/checkpoint release was already stated in v1.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly contrasts its controlled design with Conwell et al. and IT-focused prior work, removes the Huh et al. Platonic framing, and adds references for alternative objectives, datasets, software, and pretrained models. These are focused additions around a largely retained related-work account and research position.

P1.justification: The discussion is extensively expanded and reorganized, bringing training-evolution and training-objective material from appendices into named main-text subsections. v3 adds an introductory motivation paragraph, implementation and dataset appendices, and software and impact sections, while removing the Platonic subsection and rewriting parts of the limitations.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main layout and extensively rearranges and redraws figures. Figure 7 combines revised supplementary analyses; trained/random bars split into neural and behavioral panels; the pretrained display contracts from two panels to one. Regional SimCLR plots are added, the KDE display disappears, and captions and legends are revised.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the existing study through additional dataset experiments, more diagnostic saturation analyses, and substantially better documentation of auxiliary experiments. It also resolves text/figure coefficient discrepancies and the unfinished Figure 4 caption. Benefits are tempered by the loss of the separate neural-only pretrained plot and insufficiently distinguished results for the expanded pretrained/fine-tuned discussion. The net gain is useful but limited.
